patch_description: Hybrid composition of the two strongest prior programs (lag-optimized Gen 45 and smoothness-optimized Gen 46), which held 0.65 on opposite ends of the trade-off. Key insights: (1) RTS smoothing with adaptive R and 3σ robust gating gives a low-noise level+slope state; using `np.linalg.solve`-based RTS gain (rather than explicit inverse) improves numerical stability. (2) The reversal/noise bottleneck is best attacked by a *three-scale percentile-blended* SG bank: instead of sequentially convolving scales (which over-smooths and kills responsiveness), we smooth at each scale independently and blend per-sample using a percentile-based weight, so high-curvature regions retain the short-scale estimate while flat regions use the wide-scale estimate. This is the novel element — local-curvature-adaptive scale fusion. (3) Lag compensation uses a sigmoid-gated lead on the pure smoothed RTS slope (avoiding the noisier gradient blend), attenuating lead where the trend isn't statistically significant so noise cannot manufacture false reversals. (4) End-aligned trim preserves output length contract.
